name: Learn basic hand stitching
blurb: Five stitches cover nearly all hand sewing: running, backstitch, whip, slip and blanket. Once you have them, most clothing repairs become a ten-minute job.
gear: Thread in a few basic colours
steps: Learn to thread a needle, knot the end and manage thread length — too long and it tangles constantly.
Learn the running stitch for gathering and basting, keeping the stitch length even.
Learn the backstitch, the strong one, which is what you use where a seam must hold.
Learn the whip stitch for joining two edges, and the slip or ladder stitch for closing a seam invisibly.
Learn the blanket stitch for finishing raw edges decoratively.
Practise each on scrap fabric until the stitches are the same size, then do a real repair.
tips: Even stitch length is what makes hand sewing look professional. Slow down.
Use a thimble properly; it doubles the force you can apply through heavy fabric.
proof: You complete a real garment repair using at least three different stitches, chosen appropriately.
